notes.split: Chia trước mọi thử nghiệm. Dev = toàn bộ 20 câu Day 6 (q01-q20; q16-q20 là test cũ của Day 6, đã bị phân tích lỗi top-40 và gợi ý hybrid/rerank nên không còn độc lập) + 2 câu multi-hop mới + 4 câu thiếu evidence. Test = 11 câu có đáp án hoàn toàn mới (t01-t11, gồm 2 multi-hop) + 3 câu thiếu evidence mới, soạn ngày 2026-11-16 trước khi viết code retrieval/agent.
notes.types: truc_tiep, dien_dat_lai, dieu_kien, ngoai_le, metadata_filter như Day 6; multi_hop = cần evidence từ hai kỳ báo cáo.
notes.filter: filter là input người dùng chọn trước (kỳ báo cáo). Chỉ câu nêu rõ kỳ báo cáo mới có filter; câu multi-hop không có filter vì cần cả hai kỳ.
notes.gold: gold là các evidence thay thế; trường group phân nhóm evidence bắt buộc. Câu thường chỉ có group A (đủ khi có một evidence bất kỳ). Câu multi-hop có group A (bản 12/2017) và group B (bản 06/2018): đủ evidence khi mỗi group có ít nhất một evidence.
notes.answer_points: Regex các ý bắt buộc để chấm câu trả lời đúng và đủ; chỉ dùng khi chấm, không bao giờ đưa vào agent hay retrieval.
notes.leakage: Test không trùng đáp án với dev. Một số gold thay thế của test nằm ở trang Overview (ts-2017-12 tr.10-11), cũng là trang gold của vài câu dev, nhưng khác đoạn và khác đáp án.
notes.drafting: Câu mới soạn nháp với hỗ trợ của Claude Code từ text pypdf; evidence được kiểm tra tự động là nằm trọn trong một chunk đúng nguồn/trang. Học viên đã tự mở PDF đối chiếu và xác nhận toàn bộ câu mới (human_verified=true, 2026-11-16).

answerable.question: How many net new manufacturing jobs did Vietnam add over the past three years, and in what kind of sectors were these jobs mainly created?
answerable.expected_answer: About 1.6 million net new manufacturing jobs, created mainly in export-oriented sectors (such as textiles and electronics).

gold.evidence: Over the past three years Vietnam added 1.6 million new manufacturing jobs (net) - a significant pick up in manufacturing job creation. Within manufacturing, jobs were primarily created in export oriented sectors i.e. textiles and electronics.

answerable.question: How fast did average wages in Vietnam's public sector grow compared with the domestic and FDI private sector between Q1 2014 and Q1 2017, and what explains the difference?
answerable.expected_answer: Public-sector wages grew only about 3 percent on average, versus about 8.4 percent in the domestic and FDI private sector, reflecting the government's efforts to rein in the public-sector wage bill.

gold.evidence: Average monthly nominal wages in the domestic and FDI private sector grew rapidly expanding at an average rate of 8.4 percent. Meanwhile wages in the public sector grew only by an average 3 percent, reflecting the government's efforts in reining in the public-sector wage bill.

answerable.question: What share of outstanding loans did Vietnam officially report as non-performing in December 2017, and what is the estimated share once NPLs held by VAMC and potential bad debts are included?
answerable.expected_answer: Officially about 2.3 percent of total outstanding loans (December 2017); about 7.36 percent once VAMC's NPLs and potential bad debts are included.

gold.evidence: NPLs in the banking system are officially reported equivalent to 2.3 percent of total outstanding loans of the banking sector as of December 2017, however, this only partly reflects asset quality challenges in the banking system, as the measure does not include the non-performing assets held by the VAMC. Including VAMC's NPLs and potential bad debts, total non-performing assets in the banking system are estimated at about 7.36 percent.

answerable.question: Why did Vietnam's oil export earnings fall in the first four months of 2018 even though oil prices were higher?
answerable.expected_answer: Because export volumes declined substantially: oil production is constrained by technical capacity limits of Vietnam's maturing oil fields. Although oil prices rose 26.3 percent (y/y), oil export earnings contracted by 27 percent.

gold.evidence: Oil production and hence exports continue to be constrained by technical capacity constraints related to Vietnam's maturing oil fields. While oil prices are up by 26.3 percent (y/y), a substantial decline in volumes caused oil export earnings to contract by 27 percent in the first four months of 2018.
